figures.alt: Illustration of a girl in a dim classroom shining a flashlight so the beam crosses the room to a friend at her desk.
figures.caption: A flashlight beam is a pattern of light that can carry a message across a room.

figures.alt: Picture of a drum with a pile of rice grains and a wooden spoon resting on the drum skin.
figures.caption: A drum with rice grains on its skin. Tap the drum gently and watch the rice.

figures.alt: Four rows. In each, a flashlight on the left sends a beam to a material. Clear plastic: the light passes straight through. Wax paper: some light passes through and spreads out, so it is blurry. Cardboard: the light is blocked and there is a shadow behind it. Foil: the light bounces back toward the flashlight.
figures.caption: What a beam of light does to four materials: passes through, spreads, is blocked, or bounces.

figures.alt: Interactive: pluck a rubber band softly or hard, watch it vibrate and the rice jump, and touch it to stop the sound.
figures.caption: Pluck a rubber band: it shakes and makes sound. Touch it and the sound stops.

figures.alt: A flashlight on the left shines a beam onto a small red toy car, and the light bounces from the car to a child’s eye.
figures.caption: The flashlight sends light to the toy. The light bounces off the toy into your eye, so you can see it. “Light bounces into your eye.”

figures.alt: Interactive: a mystery box holds an apple or a glow star. A lamp button shows that you see the apple only when light bounces from it into your eye.
figures.caption: Turn the lamp on and off to see when you can see what is in the box.

figures.alt: Interactive: choose a material and see the flashlight beam pass through, spread out, stop with a shadow, or bounce back.
figures.caption: Shine a beam on clear plastic, wax paper, cardboard or foil.
